rules: Show the actual restored screen before proposing changes.
Discuss top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right quadrants and their control groups.
Offer small, specific options for font, size, spacing, placement, and contrast.
Keep the established artwork and character of each interface, including CritterNet.
Keep gameplay visible; do not add large opaque text panels as a default readability treatment.
Implement only the changes the user chooses for the screen under review.
Review desktop, phone, and tablet views and control hit targets before finalizing that screen.
Do not apply a chosen treatment globally without the user's direction.

gameplay_ui_review.current_screen: Home HUD, activities, furniture, and travel planner

notifications.direction: User requested a 2D sprite clipboard, legible handwritten notes, and animated page turning at the paper's lower-right corner.
notifications.verified: Desktop and Android-simulated UI interaction suites passed 695 checks each, including touch page turning. Desktop, phone, and tablet notification captures rendered; no physical-device validation.

observations: Q1 status text is small on the phone; cash has a backing but paper and sample counts do not.
Q2 date and time can land over the wall clock; Options, Exit, HUD and Notices form a two-row control cluster.
Q3 movement hints sit at the bottom and shrink on the phone beside the walking stick.
Q4 has a contextual touch action button; it is blank when no interaction is selected and reads OPEN for the office computer.
The selected-interaction prompt appears near the lower middle, outside the movement hint and action button, but becomes very small on phone.
The revised phone capture aligns the vehicle card, rescue button, and notifications to the left edge; steering is left and driving buttons and the minimap are right.
The on-foot gear button appears near the motorcycle and sits at the right edge of the wide phone view. Drawn controls and hit targets share the full viewport bounds.

The desktop full map's destination header and first place row overlap. Cause located in route_map.lua: keyRect rows reserve keyHeaderHeight only on mobile, while the desktop header is still drawn at key.y+9. This is a distinct map-layout issue for the later commute review.
The city-delivery and fuel-truck panels are separate full-screen interfaces with very small phone text, so they need their own review rather than a blanket HUD treatment.
The Home world HUD now uses the authored cash, calendar, and clock sprites with live Home and Shop balances.
The personal-needs card uses a new sprite and four pictogram icons. Home Options and HUD visibility are icons; the notifications button is an icon at the right edge.
The bottom movement and action controls retain their existing placement.
Home routines and the travel planner are separate full-screen overlays with narrow centered panels on phone and need their own quadrant review.
